issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:whitney_set_under_bilip_map inherits the hypothesis of Lemma lemma:whitney_covering_lemma, namely m(E_j) >= (1/sigma) m(B_j). The Appendix C verification of Example ex:explicit_whitney_partition establishes only m(P_{j,l}) >= (4/(27 pi)) m(B_{j,l}), which forces sigma >= 27 pi/4 (about 21.2). Instead it invokes the lemma with sigma = 4/(27 pi) < 1, for which the hypothesis would require m(E_j) >= (27 pi/4) m(B_j) > m(B_j), impossible since E_j is a subset of B_j. The lemma application is therefore invalid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the parameter sigma = 4/(27 pi) by sigma = 27 pi/4 in the application of Lemma lem:whitney_set_under_bilip_map; the hypothesis is then satisfied and the lemma yields the Whitney-set conclusion with covering constant N <= 4^n L^{3n+1} (27 pi/4) (adjusted further per ISSUE-004).
issues.overall_effect: The Appendix C verification of the explicit Whitney source-point construction announced in Example ex:explicit_whitney_partition fails as written. The example's stated conclusion (an eps'-fine Whitney set, with no numerical covering constant quoted) survives once sigma is corrected, so no labelled downstream result is lost.
issues.title: Covering lemma applied with inverted sigma in the verification of the explicit Whitney set
issues.why_classification: Single forced parameter correction; the hypothesis mismatch is immediate from E_j subset B_j, and the example's conclusion and all downstream uses survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists $\mathcal{I} \subset \N$ such that $\{q_j^+\}_{j \in \mathcal{I}}$ is a $5\varepsilon$-fine Whitney set for $\Omega^+$ with respect to $\gamma$, with covering constant $N \leq 1200$.

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of the case delta = infinity, the families of balls B'_j on which the entire lower-bound (gtrsim) argument rests (a_j = ||1||_{B'_j,k}, the Cauchy-Schwarz splitting, the Poincare-Wirtinger estimate, and the final chain) are never defined; the only balls defined in the proof are B_j = B(q_j^+, eps d(q_j^+)). Moreover, the bounded-overlap constant '400' asserted for the B'_j does not follow from Lemma lem:extracting_sub_whitney_sets, which supplies N <= 1200 for the 5eps-balls. The central discretization estimate of the main theorem is therefore ill-defined and the constant unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define B'_j = B(q_j^+, 5 eps d(q_j^+)) for j in I (the balls supplied by Lemma lem:extracting_sub_whitney_sets, which cover Omega^+ with overlap at most 1200) and replace 400 by 1200; all estimates then hold with universal constants and the theorem's statement is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:lusin_frame, the paper's main result, is incomplete as written, and with it the proof of Proposition prop:frames_for_hardy_spaces, which invokes the theorem. The statements themselves survive a local repair.
issues.title: Proof of the Lusin frame theorem uses undefined balls B'_j and an unsupported overlap constant
issues.why_classification: Local repair consisting of one forced definition plus one constant; no new argument is needed and every claim and guarantee of the theorem survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In our implementation below, we always take $\varepsilon = 0.3$.
There exists a universal constant $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that if $\varepsilon \leq \varepsilon_0$, then

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that the implemented layered source-point configuration is an eps'-fine Whitney set per Example ex:explicit_whitney_partition, and then fixes eps = 0.3. The example's hypothesis requires eps' = 3 L^2 eps / 2 <= 1/4, i.e. eps <= 1/(6 L^2) <= 1/6; at eps = 0.3 one gets eps' = 0.45 L^2 >= 0.45 > 1/4 for every domain (L >= 1), and eps' even exceeds the cap eps <= 1/2 of Definition def:whitney_set whenever L > 1.05 (both numerical test domains have L > 1). Hence the cited example does not establish the claim at the implemented parameter, and the configuration also lies far outside the regime eps <= eps_0 <= 1/20 of Theorem thm:lusin_frame, so the implemented WMFS is not covered by the paper's frame guarantees despite the abstract's 'Consequently'.

failure_location.quote: Thus $\cup_{l=N_0}^\infty \{q_{j,l}\}_{j=1}^{n_l} = \{q_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ is an $\varepsilon'$-fine Whitney set with $\varepsilon' \simeq \varepsilon$ (see Example~\ref{ex:explicit_whitney_partition}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim: state that eps = 0.3 lies outside the range verified by Example ex:explicit_whitney_partition (eps <= 1/(6 L^2)) and outside the regime eps <= eps_0 of Theorem thm:lusin_frame, so that the numerical configuration is motivated by, but not covered by, the theory; alternatively supply a new verification of the Whitney and frame properties at eps = 0.3, which the source's lemmas (capped at eps' <= 1/4 and eps <= eps_0) do not support.
issues.overall_effect: The bridge from the proven theory (frames for sufficiently fine Whitney sets) to the implemented method is unsupported: neither the Whitney-set status of the numerical source points at eps = 0.3 nor the applicability of the frame/stability theory to them is established by the paper's results.
issues.title: Implemented eps = 0.3 source configuration claimed to be a Whitney set outside the verified parameter range
issues.why_classification: No routine local repair preserves the claim: the source-supported resolution is a limited weakening that withdraws the asserted theoretical coverage of the implemented method (or a new nontrivial verification), while the theorems and the empirical numerical results themselves survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\rho : \R^n \to \R^n$ be a bi-Lipschitz map with $\mathcal{L} = \max(\textup{Lip}(\rho),\textup{Lip}(\rho^{-1}))$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims m(rho(E_j)) >= (1/L) m(E_j) for a bi-Lipschitz map rho of R^n. For n >= 2 the valid bound is m(rho(E)) >= L^{-n} m(E): a homothety z -> z/L is bi-Lipschitz with constant L and shrinks n-dimensional measure by L^n (for the paper's own radial map with r_gamma identically equal to r_0 < 1 one has L = 1/r_0 and m(rho(E)) = r_0^2 m(E) < r_0 m(E) in dimension 2). Consequently the stated covering-constant bound N <= 4^n L^{3n+1} sigma is not established; the corrected chain gives N <= 4^n L^{4n} sigma. The qualitative conclusion (the image collection is a Whitney set with finite covering constant) survives.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (1/L) m(E_j) by (1/L^n) m(E_j) in the proof and L^{3n+1} by L^{4n} in the stated bound for N; the lemma's conclusion and all downstream uses are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit covering-constant bound stated in Lemma lem:whitney_set_under_bilip_map is unreliable as stated. Since no downstream result quotes this constant (the example uses only the qualitative Whitney-set conclusion, which remains established after repair), the damage is confined to the lemma's stated numerical guarantee.
issues.title: Bi-Lipschitz volume distortion bound uses L^{-1} instead of L^{-n}
issues.why_classification: Local repair of one inequality and the resulting exponent in an unused explicit constant; the lemma's substantive conclusion and all applications survive.
